scenario.description: An office manager must finalize one catering order for a client workshop, balancing headcount, dietary needs, room access timing, and a fixed hospitality budget.

shared_context.S1: A client workshop will be held at the office next Tuesday.
shared_context.S2: Elena must place a single catering order this afternoon.
shared_context.S3: The standard menu from the preferred caterer costs $18 per person, and the boxed meal menu costs $24 per person.
shared_context.S4: The standard menu requires buffet setup access at least 45 minutes before the workshop start time, while boxed meals can be delivered 15 minutes before start time.
shared_context.S5: The current attendee list in the shared calendar shows 14 people.
shared_context.S6: Before the order is submitted, Elena does a routine round asking Client Success, Facilities, and Finance to confirm any operational details that affect the order.

PF1.text: Marcus received final confirmation from the client that 4 additional attendees will join, bringing the total headcount to 18.

PF2.text: Among the added attendees, 3 require individually labeled vegan meals, which the standard buffet menu cannot provide but the boxed meal menu can.

PF3.text: Building security approved room access for the workshop space only 20 minutes before the start time because another event occupies the room beforehand.

PF4.text: Finance approved a hospitality budget of up to $450 for this workshop.

acceptance_conditions: The order must use the boxed meal menu.
The order must cover 18 attendees.
The total cost must equal $432.
The total cost must stay within the approved hospitality budget of $450.
Client attendance growth, the vegan meal requirement, and the room-access timing constraint must all be explicitly acknowledged in the reasoning.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes the order quantity from 14 to 18, which changes the headcount field and the final total_cost number from any 14-person total to $432.
PF2 changes the menu choice from the cheaper standard buffet to boxed meals because individually labeled vegan meals are required.
PF3 changes the feasible setup option because 20-minute access makes the standard buffet impossible and leaves boxed meals as the workable choice.
PF4 sets the exact maximum budget at $450, which determines that the correct $432 order is acceptable while any padded amount above $450 fails.

scenario.description: A clinic manager must assign one clinician to cover a same-day evening urgent-care shift while balancing credential requirements, overtime rules, transportation constraints, and a promised schedule accommodation.

shared_context.S1: One clinician must be assigned today to cover the urgent-care shift from 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.
shared_context.S2: Marcus and Tara are the two available clinicians for that shift.
shared_context.S3: The shift includes the possibility of treating pediatric walk-ins.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the final coverage assignment.
shared_context.S5: The clinic tries to avoid unnecessary staffing disruptions on short notice.
shared_context.S6: Before Elena confirms the assignment, the clinic's usual practice is to have a brief scheduling huddle so the tentative plan can be discussed.

PF1.text: Marcus already worked 38 clinical hours earlier this week, and covering tonight would bring him to 42 hours; under clinic policy, any clinician scheduled above 40 hours in a week must receive a half-day off within the next 7 calendar days.

PF2.text: Tara's pediatric prescribing credential renewal was completed this morning, so she is cleared to independently handle pediatric walk-ins tonight.

PF3.text: Tara arranged childcare assuming she would finish by 5:30 p.m., but she can stay for the evening shift only if the clinic provides a taxi home after 10:00 p.m.

PF4.text: Operations promised Marcus in writing that if he covered last Saturday's emergency shift, he would not be assigned another added evening shift before next Monday unless no other qualified clinician was available.

acceptance_conditions: Tara must be assigned to the evening shift.
The assigned shift must remain 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.
The plan must state that the assigned clinician will independently handle pediatric walk-ins.
A taxi-home commitment for Tara after the shift must be included.
Marcus must not be assigned to this added evening shift.
Tara's pediatric credential renewal must be explicitly cited as part of the reasoning.
Marcus's written scheduling accommodation must be explicitly cited as part of the reasoning.
Tara's taxi requirement must be explicitly cited as part of the reasoning.

content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] == 'taxi_home' and c['target'] == 'A3' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in credited_facts

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed and decisions['assigned_clinician'] == 'A3' and decisions['pediatric_coverage_mode'] == 'independent_by_assigned_clinician'
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in revealed and decisions['assigned_clinician'] == 'A3'
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed and any(c['type'] == 'taxi_home' and c['target'] == 'A3' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes the downstream scheduling consequence of assigning Marcus by requiring a half-day off within 7 days if he covers tonight, making that option concretely more disruptive even though the final accepted settlement does not require citing PF1.
PF2 changes Tara's qualification status for pediatric walk-ins, so revealing and citing it is what makes independent pediatric coverage by Tara supportable in the final decision.
PF3 changes Tara's availability conditions by making a taxi-home commitment necessary for her to accept the evening shift, and that requirement must be revealed and cited.

PF4 changes the allowable assignment by barring Marcus from this added evening shift while another qualified clinician is available, so revealing and citing it is what makes assigning Tara instead of Marcus the correct decision.

scenario.description: A conference marketing lead must assign one company booth at an industry summit to a product line and finalize the staffing plan, balancing revenue opportunity, launch timing, staffing limits, and sponsor obligations.

shared_context.S1: The company has one 20x20 booth at the CloudScale Summit next month.
shared_context.S2: Elena will make the final decision on which product line gets the booth and how many staff badges to assign.
shared_context.S3: Product line Atlas has higher general brand recognition than product line Beacon.
shared_context.S4: The booth package includes exactly 6 staff badges unless additional badges are purchased separately.
shared_context.S5: The company wants the booth plan locked this week so design files, travel, and schedules can be finalized.
shared_context.S6: Before Elena submits the final booth request, she asks Sales, Product, and Events to give their planning inputs for the summit.

PF1.text: Sales has three qualified Beacon deals expected to close within 45 days, and each account has already booked meetings at the summit specifically to see Beacon rather than Atlas.

PF2.text: Beacon's launch slips unless the summit booth includes a live demo station with at least 4 Beacon specialists on site.

PF3.text: The summit contract requires the company to feature the product line named in its co-marketing sponsorship rider, and that named product line is Beacon.

PF4.text: Two extra staff badges can still be added for a total booth staffing capacity of 8, but the purchase deadline is tomorrow.

acceptance_conditions: Beacon must receive the booth assignment.
Total badges must equal 8.
At least 4 Beacon specialists must be assigned.
The remaining assigned booth staff must be Atlas staff, and the total assigned staff must equal the total badges.
An add-badges commitment must exist.
The sponsorship rider fact requiring Beacon must be cited from the conversation.
The Beacon staffing minimum for the live demo must be cited from the conversation.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'add_badges' and c['target'] == 'booth' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, Atlas looks like the safer choice because it has stronger general recognition; revealing PF1 changes the product choice by tying the booth to three specific Beacon revenue meetings.
PF2 sets the exact Beacon staffing minimum at 4 specialists for the live demo, which changes the staffing number and must be cited from the discussion.
PF3 changes the booth assignment by making Beacon contractually required under the sponsorship rider, and the final decision must cite that requirement from the conversation.
PF4 changes the badge count from the default 6 to 8 and requires the concrete add-badges commitment before the deadline.

scenario.description: A community festival coordinator must assign limited booth spaces and utility hookups for the weekend market.

shared_context.S1: There are three available booth spaces for the weekend market: Plaza, Fountain, and Gate.
shared_context.S2: Plaza and Fountain have electricity hookups; Gate does not.
shared_context.S3: Elena will make the final booth assignments.
shared_context.S4: Marco represents a food vendor, and Tessa represents a craft vendor.
shared_context.S5: Jordan oversees physical site setup and access rules.
shared_context.S6: Before Elena finalizes assignments, the usual planning step is for each representative to state any setup requirement or operating constraint that affects placement.
shared_context.S7: Only one vendor can be assigned to each booth space.

PF1.text: Marco's vendor uses refrigerated equipment that requires an electricity hookup and cannot operate from Gate.

PF2.text: Tessa's vendor has already printed promotional maps naming Plaza as their booth location and will incur a penalty unless assigned to Plaza.

PF3.text: A temporary water line repair will block delivery access to Plaza until noon, so no food vendor may be assigned to Plaza because food setup must be completed by 10 a.m.

acceptance_conditions: Marco must be assigned to Fountain because his vendor needs electricity and cannot use Gate, while Plaza is unavailable for food setup before opening.
Tessa must be assigned to Plaza because her printed promotional maps name Plaza as her booth location.
No two vendors may be assigned to the same booth.
Marco's electricity requirement must be explicitly credited.
Tessa's printed-map location commitment must be explicitly credited.
Jordan's blocked Plaza access for food setup must be cited in the decision rationale.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes Marco's allowable booth set by ruling out Gate and requiring an electric booth, which makes his assignment depend on a concrete utility constraint rather than a generic placement choice.
PF2 changes Tessa's required booth from any open non-conflicting spot to Plaza specifically, which determines her assignment and requires that location commitment to be credited.
PF3 rules out Plaza for Marco because food setup cannot occur there before opening, forcing Marco onto Fountain once his electricity need is also considered.

scenario.description: A department manager must choose the date and attendance plan for a required two-day training workshop that needs broad participation while staying within the approved travel budget and honoring existing obligations.

shared_context.S1: Elena must finalize one date option for the department's required two-day workshop.
shared_context.S2: The two candidate workshop windows are June 12-13 and June 19-20.
shared_context.S3: The workshop may be planned either in person or hybrid, depending on rooming, attendance coverage, and cost.
shared_context.S4: There are 18 expected attendees from the department.
shared_context.S5: The preliminary planning worksheet shows June 12-13 as the lower-cost option and June 19-20 as the higher-cost option.
shared_context.S6: Elena will make the final call after hearing each area lead's planning note on rooming, budget, and operational coverage.

PF1.text: The only room available on June 12-13 seats 14 people, while the room held on June 19-20 seats all 18 attendees.

PF2.text: Finance approved a firm maximum workshop budget of $9,250, and the booked travel quote for the feasible June 19-20 in-person plan is $8,900.

PF3.text: A contract renewal presentation with a major client is fixed on June 12, so Noah can attend the workshop only if it is scheduled on June 19-20.

acceptance_conditions: The workshop must be scheduled for June 19-20.
The workshop must be planned as in person.
The approved budget must be exactly $8,900 and must not exceed $9,250.
The plan must cover all 18 expected attendees.
The final reasoning must explicitly rely on the room-capacity fact for June 12-13 and the client-conflict fact affecting Noah's attendance.

content_checks.C5: decisions['selected_window'] == 'June 19-20' and decisions['format'] == 'in_person' and decisions['expected_attendees'] == 18 and decisions['approved_budget'] == 8900

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in revealed
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes the feasible date and format because June 12-13 cannot seat all 18 people in person, while June 19-20 can support an in-person plan for the full group.
PF2 supplies the exact approved budget number of $8,900 and the $9,250 ceiling, so the final approved_budget can be set to the required amount instead of guessed from the public planning worksheet.
PF3 changes the date choice and attendance count because June 12-13 would exclude Noah from the required workshop, while June 19-20 allows all 18 attendees to participate.
